target_refs.quote: First tenancy of the whole house was given to Onkar Nath vide Rent Note Exhibit Rw 4/7 dated 12/03/1959.
These facts would establish that sub-letting was permitted by the landlord through Onkar Nath on 12/03/1959.

element_targets.reason: The High Court treated the relevant sub-tenancy through Onkar Nath as created/permitted on 12 March 1959, which is after 9 June 1952. The frozen input contains only the appellant's post-1952 allegation and prior-occupation accounts; it does not supply the decisive 12 March 1959 rent-note timing relied on by the target court, so input_sufficient is false.

target_refs.quote: The landlord knew that these two persons Dewan Chand and Kirori Mal were already in possession and that they would be paying rent to the tenant Onkar Nath thereafter.
The reading of Exhibit Rw 4/7 shows that Kirori Mal of M/s. DesRaj Kirori Mal and Dewan Chand were allowed to be the sub-tenants of Onkar Nath.

element_targets.reason: For Dewan Chand and Kirori Mal, the High Court ultimately treated them as Onkar Nath's sub-tenants, in possession and paying rent to him, satisfying the supplied subletting-route relationship. The frozen input labels two occupants as sub-tenants but does not supply the rent-note terms showing the rent/payment incident on which the target court relied; that decisive incident is unavailable in the frozen input.

The High Court did not substantively analyze an assignment route or decide whether Onkar Nath divested himself of all tenant rights. This is an unobserved condition, not an evidentiary UNRESOLVED finding.

The High Court did not separately adjudicate the supplied parting-with-possession route requiring divestment or abandonment of the tenant's own right to possession. Its operative analysis proceeded on subletting and written consent.

target_refs.quote: Exhibit Rw 4/7 amply proves that the landlord gave his consent in writing to the sub-letting and notice of the creation of sub-tenancy duly served on the landlord.
Since this Court is of the view that the document Exhibit RW4/7 is a written consent to the landlord/owner and a notice of creation of subtenancy, hence appeal must fail.

element_targets.reason: The GIVEN condition is lack of written consent. The High Court affirmatively found the opposite: Exhibit RW4/7 constituted the landlord's written consent to the subletting. The frozen input contains a prior finding of landlord consent and a claimed rent note, but not the decisive signatures/terms establishing consent in writing, so the historic target finding depends on evidence unavailable from the frozen input.
The High Court did not apply the concurrent-use/legal-possession qualification for a parting-with-possession route. No explicit evidentiary issue on this condition was left unresolved.

cases.procedural_outcome_separate: The Delhi High Court dismissed the landlord's second appeal and left the Rent Control Tribunal's dismissal of the eviction petition undisturbed.
coverage_limits: The affirmative subletting-route findings for DRC_SUBLETTING_C01 and DRC_SUBLETTING_C02 concern the court's treatment of Dewan Chand and Kirori Mal as sub-tenants through Onkar Nath; the judgment separately upheld findings of no subletting as to other named occupants.
Assignment and parting-with-possession were not separately adjudicated under the supplied retrospective decomposition.
The input_sufficient flags are assessed only against the separately frozen input and do not import target-stage facts into that input.

target_refs.quote: And in fact, the finding of the Rent Control Tribunal at paragraph '61' categorically records that there is no material on record to show that the sub-tenancy dates back prior to 09.06.1952.
This Court is unable to accept the contention of the Petitioner that the sub-tenancy in its favour was created in 1944 as contended during oral arguments.

element_targets.reason: The High Court rejected the petitioner's newly raised 1944 factual plea and relied on the record finding that there was no material showing a pre-9 June 1952 sub-tenancy. It therefore treated the statutory post-cutoff condition as satisfied for the case, but this was a burden/record determination rather than an affirmative historical finding of the exact creation date; fact_truth remains UNKNOWN. The frozen input contains both the 1944 claim and the prior finding that no case or document showed a pre-cutoff sub-tenancy, so it is sufficient for this target.

target_refs.quote: The Petitioner fairly admitted that the Petitioner did not act upon the offer in letter dated 29.05.2001 and did not attorn in favour of Respondent No.1 (landlord); and continued to pay rent only to Respondent No. 2 (Canara Bank).
The Petitioner's landlord was therefore Respondent No. 2 i.e., Canara Bank alone.

element_targets.reason: The High Court expressly treated United India Insurance Co. Ltd. as a sub-tenant whose landlord remained Canara Bank, with rent continuing to be paid to Canara Bank. That is a substantive subletting-route finding. Although the target court discussed additional letters, the frozen input already contains the Rent Control Tribunal's pre-target finding that Canara Bank sub-let the property to the Petitioner, which the target court ultimately left standing and treated as applicable.
The High Court did not substantively decide an assignment route or whether Canara Bank divested itself of all rights held as tenant.
The High Court did not separately adjudicate the supplied parting-with-possession route requiring divestment or abandonment of Canara Bank's own right to possession.

target_refs.quote: The Coordinate Bench in the judgement dated 12.04.2023 passed in CM(M) 336/2023 returned the following findings, which bind the Petitioner herein as well, in the facts of this case: -

>  (iii) Knowledge of the existence of the sub-tenants is of no consequence in view of the mandatory provision of cite16†Section 17 read with cite15†Section 18 of the DRC Act as there is no document evidencing the consent of Respondent No. 1, landlord for creation of the sub-tenancy.
In the opinion of this Court, the aforesaid findings of the Coordinate Bench apply with all fours to the present Petitioner.

element_targets.reason: The High Court expressly adopted as binding and applicable the finding that there was no document evidencing the landlord's consent to creation of the sub-tenancy. That legally satisfies the GIVEN lack-of-written-consent condition, but because the reasoning is failure of proof rather than an affirmative historical finding that consent never existed, fact_truth remains UNKNOWN. The frozen input already contains the Rent Control Tribunal's pre-target finding that no written consent was obtained, so input_sufficient is true.

The High Court did not apply the concurrent-use/legal-possession qualification as a separate parting-with-possession determination. The licensee theory appeared in the parties' earlier pleadings, but the target court did not substantively resolve this GIVEN qualification.

cases.procedural_outcome_separate: The Delhi High Court dismissed the Article 227 petition, held the Coordinate Bench's prior findings applicable to the Petitioner on all fours, and left the Rent Control Tribunal's eviction order undisturbed.
coverage_limits: The target court's reasoning is specific to United India Insurance Co. Ltd. as the remaining petitioner/sub-tenant and also expressly adopts Coordinate Bench findings concerning the same lease and other sub-tenants.

DRC_SUBLETTING_C01 is treated as legally satisfied because the pre-1952 defence was not accepted; the target court did not affirmatively determine the exact historical creation date, so fact_truth is UNKNOWN rather than TRUE.

DRC_SUBLETTING_C05 is based on failure to prove written consent and adopted prior findings; it is not converted into a factual assertion that consent was historically impossible or definitively absent.
Assignment and parting-with-possession routes were not separately adjudicated under the supplied retrospective decomposition.
